ch-canton-18.atlas_note: Switzerland's Pinot Noir stronghold: two thirds of the vines are Blauburgunder. The warm Föhn wind from the south, called the grape cooker, gives long ripe autumns in a valley sheltered by the Rätikon. Four villages of the Bündner Herrschaft hold about 83% of the vineyards. The law names three wine areas: the Bündner Rheintal, the Misox south of the Alps and Brusio in the Valposchiavo.

ch-canton-21.atlas_note: The wine canton of Italian-speaking Switzerland, and Merlot country: about three quarters of the vines are Merlot. It came after phylloxera, when the first cuttings were handed out in 1906 and Bondola, the old local red, was replaced. The Monte Ceneri pass splits the canton into the Sopraceneri and the Sottoceneri, and the Mendrisio district alone has over a third of the vines. Nearly a third of the Merlot is now pressed as white wine.
ch-canton-21.vine_area_note: 88% red, 12% white, 2025, canton Ticino only. With the Mesolcina the cantonal office counts 1,143 ha for Italian-speaking Switzerland in 2025, of which 855 ha (74.8%) Merlot.
ch-canton-21.basis: Regolamento sulla viticoltura (RViti), RL 916.150 of 11 Sept 2024, art. 16 to 18, and the Direttive sulla viticoltura of 13 Sept 2024 (point 3, DOC; point 5, IGT), on the federal Weinverordnung SR 916.140. The 2015 regulation, which held the DOC rules, was repealed in 2024.
ch-canton-21.label_rule: 'Ticino' plus a grape variety: at least 90% of that variety. Blends: 'Rosso, Bianco or Rosato del Ticino', naming the main variety and others above 10%, never a single variety. 'Denominazione di origine controllata' in full on the main label, right after the name. Part of canton, district, commune, frazione or land register name may be added if on the production and harvest control certificates; not on non-vintage DOC in 1, 0.5 or 0.2 l bottles with crown or screw cap. 'Castello' only for land with that name in the land register for 20 years. Riserva needs the vintage (Direttive 2024, 3.1, 3.10, 3.13, 3.14).
ch-canton-21.grapes: Red: Bondola / Cabernet Franc / Cabernet Sauvignon / Carminoir / Diolinoir / Divico / Galotta / Gamaret / Garanoir / Marselan / Merlot / Petit Verdot / Pinot Nero / Syrah. Up to 10% of other registered varieties, not named on the label.

rules: Nostrano is a traditional name of the IGT tier, not DOC. Any variety registered in the vineyard cadastre of Ticino or the Mesolcina may be used, including the American and hybrid grapes that are banned from DOC blending and from other IGT wine (RViti 2024 art. 18; Direttive 2024 point 5 and annex 1). Swiss Wine notes Bondola is often blended into Nostrano.

Americana is the local name for American grapes and direct-producer hybrids such as Isabella, Clinton and Noah. Annex 1 of the 2024 directives excludes them from DOC and from IGT, except as Nostrano. The 2024 statistics count 42.9 ha of red American and hybrid varieties plus 4.8 ha of Isabella in the canton, most of it in the Locarnese, the Luganese and the Valle Maggia.

Much Merlot is pressed as a white wine. In 2023, 1,491,354 kg of Merlot, 29% of the Merlot harvest, was vinified white; in 2024, 43.4 ha were registered as Merlot for Blanc de Noir. The law has no separate category for it: it is DOC Ticino like any other white, and growers must declare red grapes vinified white (RViti 2024 art. 11).

DOC grapes may come from Ticino and the Mesolcina (GR) and must be vinified in Ticino or the Mesolcina. Minimum natural sugar 18.0 Brix for red and 16.0 Brix for white; maximum yield 1,000 g/m2 red and 1,200 g/m2 white. Up to 10% blending, never with red or rosé wine from outside the canton (Direttive 2024, 3.3 to 3.8).
Growers in Ticino 2023, including 111 from outside the canton with vines in Ticino; plus 93 in the Mesolcina. 185 wineries vinified grapes in 2023 (Rapporto vendemmia 2023).
2025: 37,903 hl of wine in Ticino, 14,003 hl white and 23,900 hl red; 10,240 hl of the white was made from red grapes (BLW, Das Weinjahr 2025).

ch-canton-22.atlas_note: The second wine canton of Switzerland and the home of Chasselas. Six regional AOCs, Chablais, Lavaux, La Côte, Côtes de l'Orbe, Bonvillars and Vully, and two grand cru appellations, Dézaley and Calamin, inside Lavaux. The terraces of Lavaux are a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2007. Since 2010 the best parcels can earn the cantonal mention Premier grand cru.
ch-canton-22.grape_share_note: Chasselas about 60% of the area in 2018, down from 71% in 1994 (Statistique Vaud, Numerus 2019)
ch-canton-22.basis: Règlement sur les vins vaudois (RVV), RSV 916.125.2

ch-canton-23.atlas_note: The largest wine canton of Switzerland, about a third of the national vineyard, along the dry upper Rhône valley from Lake Geneva to Brig. Pinot Noir, Chasselas sold as Fendant and Gamay cover half the vines; Sylvaner, Petite Arvine, Heida, Syrah, Cornalin and Humagne Rouge follow. There is one cantonal AOC. Below it a wine can name its commune, and a dozen communes have their own Grand Cru rules. The law knows no premier cru: the word is banned on Valais labels.
ch-canton-23.vine_area_note: 45,777,472 m2 in 2025: 1,931.6 ha white (42%) and 2,646.1 ha red (58%), down 38 ha on 2024 (BLW). The cantonal wine office gives 4,564 ha and 62 wine communes on its own page. About 18,225 people own vineyard in the register.
ch-canton-23.grape_share_note: Hectares for Valais in BLW, Das Weinjahr 2025, tables 1.2 and 1.3 (given there in ares). The canton page gives Pinot Noir 26.6%, Chasselas 16.0% and Gamay 9.4%, together 52% of the vineyard. Amigne, Humagne Blanche, Humagne Rouge and Cornalin are grown almost only in Valais.
ch-canton-23.basis: Ordonnance sur la vigne et le vin (OVV), RS VS 916.142, of 17 March 2004 (consolidated version in force 1 April 2026)
ch-canton-23.label_rule: Commune name on the label: at least 85% of the grapes from the commune and the rest from neighbouring communes; 'Ville de' or 'Village de' may precede it (OVV art. 63). Neighbouring communes with a uniform natural setting may share a regional name with the service's approval, but names like 'district de Sion' are banned (art. 64). A local name from the official survey may be used (art. 68).

rules: Grand Cru (OVV art. 85 to 97): set by a communal or regional regulation homologated by the Conseil d'Etat, one per commune or region. Only Chasselas, Sylvaner, Amigne, Arvine, Marsanne, Roussanne, Savagnin, Humagne Blanc, Pinot Gris, Rèze, Pinot Noir, Gamay, Cornalin, Humagne Rouge and Syrah. Yield at most 1.1 kg/m2 for Chasselas, 1.0 for Sylvaner, 0.8 for the rest; vines at least eight years old; no blending of varieties or vintages; vinified and bottled in Valais. The label shows Grand Cru, the commune or region and the vintage; 'Grand Cru Valais', 'premier cru' and 'cru classé' are banned. Cornalin, Humagne Rouge and Syrah not before 1 April of the second year. The IVV control rules add the common Valais bottle and a tasting minimum of 84/100.

Fendant = Chasselas, Johannisberg = Sylvaner, Malvoisie = Pinot Gris, Ermitage = Marsanne and/or Roussanne, Païen or Heida = Savagnin Blanc, Dôle = Pinot Noir alone or at least 85% Pinot Noir with Gamay, Dôle Blanche and Oeil de Perdrix are rosés, Goron is a red vin de pays without place name (OVV art. 49 to 61)

ch-canton-24.atlas_note: About 600 ha on the north shore of Lake Neuchâtel, at the foot of the Jura, from Le Landeron to Vaumarcus. Limestone soils of Jurassic origin. Pinot Noir covers more than half the vineyard, Chasselas about a quarter. Only twelve grape varieties are allowed for the AOC. The canton gave the country the Œil-de-Perdrix rosé and the unfiltered Chasselas sold each January.
ch-canton-24.vine_area_note: 382.8 ha red (63%) and 220.5 ha white (37%), 2025. The legal vineyard zone (zone viticole) was enlarged to 556 ha in March 2018 (Plan directeur cantonal, fiche S_23).

ch-canton-24.label_rule: One AOC, Neuchâtel. A commune, locality, region or sector name may be added if at least 85% of the grapes come from it (art. 4); a cadastral name needs 95% from parcels of that name (art. 5). The grape must be named, except for Chasselas, Pinot Noir and sparkling wine (art. 6). A Pinot Noir must hold at least 95% Pinot Noir (art. 12). Wines must be made in the canton (art. 15).
ch-canton-24.producers_note: 53 winegrowers and cellars (Neuchâtel Vins et Terroir). Caves de la Ville de Neuchâtel own 13.4 ha (Hachette Vins).

rules: Grand cru is governed by a regulation of the Interprofession viti-vinicole neuchâteloise (IVN). Only still AOC Neuchâtel wines made solely from Chardonnay, Chasselas or Pinot Noir vinified red may use it. Any other quality term such as 1er Cru or Grand cru classé is banned (RSN 916.120.1 art. 14).

Minimum sugar 15.2 °Brix for Chasselas and Müller-Thurgau, 18.4 °Brix for most other still wines (annex 2). Maximum yield 0.9 kg/m² for Chasselas and Müller-Thurgau, 0.8 kg/m² for most others, 1.0 kg/m² for sparkling base (annex 3, 2021).

Chasselas AOC Neuchâtel bottled without any filtration, sold from the third Wednesday of January after the harvest (RSN 916.120.1 annex 7). First made in 1975 by Henri-Alexandre Godet. About thirty cellars make it, about 15% of the canton's Chasselas (Neuchâtel Vins et Terroir 2024).

Federal term: rosé AOC wine from Pinot Noir, with at most 10% Pinot Gris or Pinot Blanc (Ordonnance sur le vin RS 916.140, annex 1). Not reserved to Neuchâtel. First official trace in Neuchâtel 1861, a label printed by Louis Bovet, cellar owner at Areuse.

Blanc de noirs from Pinot Noir. Protected as the guarantee mark Perdrix blanche®; the 2010 AOC decree barred blending and tied its making to the mark's rules (art. 10 and 11). Not named in the 2016 decree.

ch-canton-25.atlas_note: The first AOC of Switzerland, created in 1988, and the third wine canton. Three areas: the Rive droite or Mandement with Satigny, the largest wine commune of the country, Entre Arve et Rhône and Entre Arve et Lac. Gamay, not Chasselas, is the first grape. Half the vineyard is in 23 premiers crus, defined parcels of at least about 1 ha with lower yields.
ch-canton-25.vine_area_note: 1,246.3 ha in Switzerland and 117.4 ha in the French border zone (Viry, Challex, Saint-Julien and others), 2024. 56% red.

Single-variety whites other than Chasselas must name the grape, blends say Assemblage de cépages (art. 20a). Sweetening of AOC wine is banned since 1 July 2015.
ch-canton-10.atlas_note: Two small vineyards on the Three Lakes. The Vully on the Mont Vully between Lake Morat and Lake Neuchâtel, shared with Vaud, and Cheyres on the south shore of Lake Neuchâtel. Chasselas is the first grape, then Pinot Noir. The Freiburger, a cross also called Freisamer, is a Vully speciality.

ch-canton-2.atlas_note: Two wine regions by law, Lake Biel and Lake Thun, plus scattered vineyards elsewhere in the canton. Nearly nine tenths of the vines are on the north-west shore of Lake Biel and the Jolimont. The cantonal law leaves the AOC rules to two growers' societies, the Rebgesellschaft Bielersee and the Rebgesellschaft Thunersee-Bern.

ch-reg-gr-rheintal.atlas_note: The Rhine valley from Fläsch on the St. Gallen border up to Bonaduz, with almost all the vines of the canton. Most of them lie on the right bank of the Rhine, on calcareous slate scree. The Bündner Herrschaft in the north is the heart of it, the Churer Rheintal around Chur the smaller rest.
ch-reg-gr-rheintal.grapes: Pinot Noir / Müller-Thurgau / Chardonnay / Pinot Blanc / Sauvignon Blanc / Pinot Gris / Completer

ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.basis: Official production area under the 2002 ordinance (Art. 17); since 2018 the law names only the Bündner Rheintal. Labels name the village: Fläscher, Maienfelder, Jeninser, Malanser.
ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.atlas_note: Four villages under the Falknis and the Rätikon, the best known Pinot Noir address of Switzerland. Pinot Noir came from Burgundy around 1630, probably with Bündner mercenaries, and Schloss Salenegg in Maienfeld has made wine since 1068. The Föhn, the warm dry wind from the south, ripens the grapes late into autumn, and the vines sit at about 500 to 650 m on calcareous slate scree. Malans keeps the Completer, a white grape first written down there in 1321.
ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.grape_share_note: Pinot Noir: 235.1 of 351.8 ha, Plantahof Rebbaustatistik 2025
ch-reg-gr-herrschaft.producers_note: Gantenbein, Adank, Christian and Roman Hermann, Marugg and Davaz in Fläsch; Donatsch, Wegelin, Boner, Fromm, Liesch and Studach in Malans; Eichholz and Obrecht in Jenins; Schloss Salenegg in Maienfeld (Falstaff guide)

ch-reg-gr-flaesch.atlas_note: The northernmost village of Graubünden, under the Fläscherberg on the St. Gallen border. Small, with a tight group of family estates such as Gantenbein, Adank, Hermann, Marugg and Davaz.

ch-reg-gr-maienfeld.atlas_note: The largest wine commune of the canton, with the most growers. Schloss Salenegg here has made wine since 1068.

ch-reg-vd-chablais.atlas_note: The upper Rhône valley between the end of Lake Geneva and the Valais. Chasselas from Yvorne, Aigle, Ollon and Bex is the classic, and the Föhn warms and dries the grapes in autumn. Villeneuve at the lake end is the gateway. In 2012 a Premier grand cru from Yvorne, L'Ovaille 1584, became the first wine of the Vaud government.

ch-reg-be-bielersee.atlas_note: Vines on the steep south-east facing shore of Lake Biel from Vingelz through Tüscherz, Twann and Ligerz to Schafis and La Neuveville, and on the Jolimont around Erlach, Tschugg, Gampelen and Ins. ch-reg-fr-vully.basis: RSF 912.4.111 art. 13 al. 1 let. a and art. 16 al. 2: the Vully vineyard is the grape-growing area of Mont-Vully (FR) and Vully-les-Lacs (VD)

ch-reg-fr-vully.atlas_note: The Fribourg side of the Mont Vully, two thirds of the appellation. Vines on molasse benches facing Lake Morat. Chasselas leads, then Pinot Noir. Freiburger and Traminer are local specialities. The commune of Mont-Vully replaced Bas-Vully and Haut-Vully in the ordinance text.
